body: https://konard.github.io/network/?code=2222&rotation=90&turns=15+-15&gaps=0.18+0.18+%7E+%7E&lang=en If I use auto mode and omit angles I kind of works: https://konard.github.io/network/?code=2222&rotation=90&solve=true&gaps=0.18+0.18+%7E+%7E&lang=en But if I removed gaps settings which were set manually it does not work: It should have been searching for gap configuration which reduces overlap, and also finds nearest configuration to specific padding/margin between all drawn shapes/paths and so on. So `https://konard.github.io/network/?code=2222&rotation=90&turns=15+-15&gaps=0.18+0.18+%7E+%7E&lang=en` can be added as test case of perfect arrangement. Yet it may be done even perfect, if the arrow is sharp (not rounded) - this also should be configurable if not yet. We should make nice per link configuration editor, so it is easy to edit each configuration for each link, and we should use list of cards for each links where we put all inputs, so no expandable section is needed for per link configuration. Also if angle of arrow is too small it stops being pointy, and becomes rounded that is a bug. Also we should be able to make by default pointy arrow, that makes the line shorter, so both start and end of top link in the example would land on the same line in this configuration. At the moment the right pointy arrow is a little bit longer or closer to other bottom link. Yet for both gap is 0.18 and 0.18, which is not correct. That behavior should be optional (disablable by default), to be able to keep backwards compatibility if needed, by by default we should make sure if the arrow is pointy we do line little bit shorter, so if we compare start and end of the link in length from middle to start/end their length is the same and `0.18 and 0.18` with same angles will land them on exactly the same horizontal line in this case. We need to download all logs and data related about the issue to this repository, make sure we compile that data to `./docs/case-studies/issue-{id}` folder, and use it to do deep case study analysis (also make sure to search online for additional facts and data), in which we will reconstruct timeline/sequence of events, list of each and all requirements from the issue, find root causes of the each problem, and propose possible solutions and solution plans for each requirement (we should also check known existing components/libraries, that solve similar problem or can help in solutions). If there is not enough data to find actual root cause, add debug output and verbose mode if not present, that will allow us to find root cause on next iteration.
